title: Rotate Array
spaceBreakdown:
- int variables n, k, l, r, tmp: constant → O(1)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input vector nums (modified in place)
approach: Rotate right by k means the last k elements move to the front. We can achieve this in-place with three reversals: (1) reverse the entire array, (2) reverse the first k elements, (3) reverse the remaining n−k elements. Before doing anything, reduce k modulo n so that k ≥ n or k = 0 are handled correctly. Each reversal is O(n), and we use only a handful of index variables, so the solution is O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
hints: When [1,2,3,4,5,6,7] is rotated right by 3 to get [5,6,7,1,2,3,4], which elements from the input now occupy the first 3 positions, and did their relative order change?
Use three array reversals. Reverse the whole array [1,2,3,4,5,6,7] → [7,6,5,4,3,2,1], then reverse the first k=3 → [5,6,7,4,3,2,1], then reverse the remaining 4 → [5,6,7,1,2,3,4].

```
k = k mod n
if k == 0: return
reverse(nums, 0, n-1)
reverse(nums, 0, k-1)
reverse(nums, k, n-1)
```

**Single element** - n = 1, any k is a no-op after modulo
`Input: nums = [42], k = 5` → `Expected: [42]`
⚠️ Bug: skipping k %= n → reverse(nums, 0, 4) reads past end → undefined behavior

**k exceeds n** - k must be reduced modulo n before indexing
`Input: nums = [1,2,3,4,5,6,7], k = 10` → `Expected: [6,7,1,2,3,4,5]`
⚠️ Bug: skipping k %= n → reverse(nums, 0, 9) accesses index 9 in a 7-element array → out of bounds

**Wrong reversal order** - reversing subarrays before the full array
`Input: nums = [1,2,3,4,5,6,7], k = 3` → `Expected: [5,6,7,1,2,3,4]`
⚠️ Bug: reversing first k, then last n−k, then all → returns [4,5,6,7,1,2,3]

**Off-by-one in reversal range** - using k instead of k−1 as the end index
`Input: nums = [1,2,3,4,5], k = 4` → `Expected: [2,3,4,5,1]`
⚠️ Bug: reverse(nums, 0, k) instead of reverse(nums, 0, k−1) → returns [1,2,3,4,5]

followUps.q: How would you rotate the array to the left by k steps instead?
followUps.a: Rotating left by k is equivalent to rotating right by n−k. Replace k with (n−k) mod n and apply the same three-reversal technique. Time remains O(n), space O(1).

followUps.q: How would you handle rotation if the array is given as a singly linked list?
followUps.a: Compute the length in one pass, then advance to the (n−k)-th node, detach the tail, and reconnect it to the head. This takes one or two passes with O(1) extra pointers. Time O(n), space O(1).

followUps.q: Can you solve this in-place with O(1) extra space using a different technique?
followUps.a: Use cyclic replacements: start at index 0, move each element to its target position (i+k) mod n, saving the displaced element, and repeat until you cycle back. Then advance to the next unvisited start index. Time O(n), space O(1).
